title: 8-9. FEW AND DIFFICULT HAVE BEEN MY YEARS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Pharaoh asked him, 'How old are you?' And Jacob said to Pharaoh, 'The years of my pilgrimage are a hundred and thirty. My years have been few and difficult, and they do not equal the years of the pilgrimage of my fathers.'" — Gen 47:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the most honest verses in Genesis. A hundred and thirty years old, and Jacob's summary of his life is: few and difficult.

He is not exaggerating. He fled from a brother who wanted to kill him. He was cheated repeatedly by his uncle. He buried Rachel on a roadside. He grieved a son he believed had been torn apart by animals. He lived through famine. Much of the trouble he brought on himself through deception, and he knows it.

There is no pretending here, and Scripture does not rebuke him for it. The Bible never asks us to perform contentment we do not feel. The Psalms are full of people telling God the truth about how hard life has been.

But notice the word Jacob uses twice: pilgrimage. Not "my life" — my pilgrimage. He understands that he has been travelling, not settling. Even a difficult journey is going somewhere.

That is the honest Christian posture. We can say plainly that life has been hard, and still say we are on our way home. Paul held both together: outwardly wasting away, inwardly being renewed day by day, with troubles that are light compared to what is coming (2 Cor 4:16-17).

You are allowed to say it has been hard. Just do not forget you are on a pilgrimage.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you be honest with God about how hard things have been?
2. Does thinking of your life as a pilgrimage change how you see this season?
3. Where do you need renewing inwardly today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I will not pretend with You. Some of my years have been hard. Thank You that I am on a pilgrimage and not lost, and that You are renewing me even when I feel worn down. Amen.
